findings.title: Species-level detection mostly survives
findings.text: Mean class AUC 0.985 on focal vs 0.930 on soundscape; 13 of 14 species keep AUC ≥ 0.90 on soundscapes. foxspa collapses (AUC drops by 0.33).

evidence.method: Class ROC-AUC of the model's sigmoid output for the species, on all focal clips (negatives = other species) and all 12,000 soundscape clips.

findings.title: Prototypes transfer unevenly
findings.text: 29 of 70 prototypes lose more than 0.1 detection AUC on soundscapes while 9 improve; in 8 of 14 species the best- and worst-transferring prototypes differ by ≥ 0.15 AUC.

evidence.method: ΔAUC = soundscape − focal ROC-AUC of each prototype's max activation as a detector of its own species. Spread = max − min ΔAUC among a species' prototypes.

findings.title: Activations shrink, ranking survives
findings.text: On clips with the species, the median soundscape activation is 39% of the focal one (pooled medians 0.27 → 0.10). On clips without it, activations stay near zero (84% ≤ 0.05), so positives still rank above negatives: median prototype AUC on soundscapes is 0.87.

evidence.method: Each entry is one prototype's max activation on one clip, pooled over the 70 prototypes of the analysed species. Positives = clips labelled with the prototype's species. n = focal_pos 15,520, focal_neg 366,680, soundscape_pos 31,125, soundscape_neg 808,875.

findings.title: Evidence shares are stable, but the top prototype often changes
findings.text: Each prototype's share of the class evidence correlates across domains (r = 0.81, mean change 4.6 points), yet the top prototype is the same in only 6 of 14 species. Largest shifts: foxspa P1 20%→40%, moublu P1 22%→36%, whcspa P3 19%→30%.

stats: Species with the same top prototype
evidence.method: Share = mean over positive clips of w_k·a_k / Σ_j w_j·a_j (w = non-negative last-layer weight, a = max activation): the fraction of the class logit (minus bias) from prototype k.

findings.title: Failing prototypes drift to the noise floor
findings.text: 5 prototypes that fire at bird-song frequencies (> 1 kHz) on focal clips peak in the lowest band (~0.1 kHz, wind/ambient) on soundscapes: whcspa P1, whcspa P5, clanut P5, herthr P4, daejun P2. Their AUC changes by -0.17 on average vs -0.08 for the rest.

evidence.method: Peak = median (over positive clips) of the frequency row where the prototype's activation map is maximal; rows are 16 mel bins wide (lowest row centred at ~0.1 kHz).

findings.title: Some prototypes match the same acoustic part in both domains
findings.text: whcspa P3 (a pure-tone note) and P4 (a trill) fire on the same structures in focal and soundscape clips and keep soundscape AUC above 0.9. P5's best soundscape matches also resemble its focal ones, but they are rare: its median soundscape activation is ~0 and its AUC drops to 0.67.

evidence.method: Visual inspection of the top-3 activating patches per domain (crop = peak cell ± 2 grid cells), checked against each prototype's AUC and median activation on all positive clips (table).

findings.title: Others latch onto noise in soundscapes
findings.text: whcspa P2's top soundscape matches are broadband noise bursts around 6 kHz rather than song: high activation there is likely spurious.

evidence.method: Visual inspection of the top-3 activating patches per domain. Note P2 still has soundscape AUC 0.91: the spurious matches are among its strongest activations, not the majority of its detections.

caveats: Focal clips are Xeno-Canto recordings, which are part of the model's XCL training data: focal numbers are an in-domain reference, not a held-out score.
Species with fewer than 30 soundscape positives have noisy soundscape statistics.
Prototype AUC uses the prototype's max activation as a detector of its own species (focal negatives = other species' focal clips; soundscape negatives = all other soundscape clips).
